title: Bienvenue dans notre laboratoire scientifique
oneGoal: Students will identify the classroom science area as a special place for discovery and learning
decisionPoints: What science area features should students notice first (tools, materials, safety signs)?
Should we introduce the word 'laboratoire' or use simpler terms like 'coin sciences'?
Are students ready for basic lab rules or should we start with exploration?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes the science learning environment and builds excitement for scientific inquiry
realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists work in special places with special tools, just like doctors or chefs

title: Nos règles de sécurité en sciences
oneGoal: Students will learn and practice three basic safety rules for science activities: listen, look, and be careful
decisionPoints: Which safety rules are most important for Grade 1 science activities?
Should we use visual cues or verbal rules for safety reminders?
Are students ready for practicing safety scenarios or should we model behaviors?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by establishing essential safety foundations for all future science learning
realWorldConnection: Learning that safety rules help us have fun and stay safe, like wearing seatbelts in cars

title: Observer avec nos yeux de scientifiques
oneGoal: Students will practice careful observation skills using only their eyes to notice details about objects
decisionPoints: What objects are most interesting for developing observation skills?
Should we observe one object together or let students choose their own?
Are students ready for describing what they see or should we start with pointing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by developing the fundamental skill of scientific observation through sight
realWorldConnection: Using careful looking to notice things around us, like watching for changes in the weather

title: Écouter comme des scientifiques
oneGoal: Students will use their sense of hearing to gather information about different objects and materials
decisionPoints: Which sound-making activities are safe and engaging for classroom use?
Should we focus on loud/quiet or different types of sounds?
Are students ready for sound descriptions or should we start with simple comparisons?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by expanding observation skills to include auditory information gathering
realWorldConnection: Understanding how listening carefully helps us learn, like hearing if something is working properly

title: Sentir en sécurité
oneGoal: Students will learn when and how to safely use their sense of smell in science investigations
decisionPoints: Which scents are safe and appropriate for classroom smell investigations?
Should we use prepared scent containers or natural materials?
Are students ready for smell safety rules or should we model safe smelling?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by adding smell to observation skills while emphasizing safety protocols
realWorldConnection: Learning that some smells tell us about safety, like smelling food to know if it's fresh

title: Toucher avec précaution
oneGoal: Students will learn safe touching techniques for science exploration and when NOT to touch
decisionPoints: What materials provide safe, interesting texture experiences for students?
Should we establish 'no-touch' rules for certain items or focus on safe touching?
Are students ready for texture vocabulary or should we start with simple descriptions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by completing the five senses approach to safe scientific observation
realWorldConnection: Understanding when it's safe to touch things and when we need to be careful, like petting friendly animals

title: Nos outils de scientifiques
oneGoal: Students will identify and name basic science tools: magnifying glass, ruler, and measuring cups
decisionPoints: Which science tools are safest and most engaging for Grade 1 students?
Should we introduce all tools at once or focus on one tool per lesson?
Are students ready for tool safety rules or should we model proper use?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by introducing tools that enhance scientific observation and measurement
realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists use special tools to see and measure better, like how doctors use stethoscopes

title: Explorer avec une loupe
oneGoal: Students will use magnifying glasses safely to observe small details in familiar objects
decisionPoints: What objects reveal interesting details when magnified for Grade 1 students?
Should students work with individual loupes or share in small groups?
Are students ready for independent magnifying glass use or need guided practice?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by providing hands-on experience with the most engaging science tool for young learners
realWorldConnection: Understanding how magnifying glasses help us see tiny things, like looking at insects or reading small print

title: Mesurer avec des outils
oneGoal: Students will use simple measuring tools to compare sizes and amounts of classroom objects
decisionPoints: Which measuring activities are most concrete and successful for Grade 1 students?
Should we use standard tools (rulers) or non-standard tools (blocks, hands)?
Are students ready for recording measurements or should we focus on comparing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by introducing measurement as another way scientists gather information about objects
realWorldConnection: Understanding how we measure things in daily life, like checking if clothes fit or measuring ingredients

title: Dessiner nos observations
oneGoal: Students will create simple drawings to record what they observe during science investigations
decisionPoints: What objects are easiest for students to draw and observe simultaneously?
Should we provide drawing templates or encourage free-form scientific drawings?
Are students ready for detailed drawings or should we focus on basic shapes and features?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by introducing scientific recording through drawing, a natural skill for Grade 1 students
realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists keep track of what they discover by drawing, like how we draw pictures of family trips

title: Trier et classer nos découvertes
oneGoal: Students will sort objects into groups based on observable characteristics like color, size, or texture
decisionPoints: Which classification criteria are most obvious and engaging for Grade 1 students?
Should students sort independently or work together in guided groups?
Are students ready for explaining their sorting choices or should we focus on the action of sorting?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by introducing classification as a fundamental scientific thinking skill
realWorldConnection: Understanding how we organize things at home by putting similar items together, like toys in bins

title: Prédire et vérifier
oneGoal: Students will make simple predictions about what might happen and then test their ideas safely
decisionPoints: What prediction activities are safe and have clear, observable outcomes for students?
Should we start with obvious predictions or challenge students with less predictable outcomes?
Are students ready for explaining why they made specific predictions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by introducing scientific thinking through prediction and testing
realWorldConnection: Understanding that we often guess what will happen before we try something, like predicting weather or game outcomes

title: Expérience simple avec l'eau
oneGoal: Students will conduct a safe, simple water experiment while following established safety and observation protocols
decisionPoints: Which water experiments are safest and most engaging for classroom use?
Should we focus on floating/sinking, mixing, or temperature observations?
Are students ready for independent experiment steps or need guided practice?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by combining safety rules, observation skills, and scientific tools in a hands-on experiment
realWorldConnection: Understanding that experiments help us learn by trying things safely, like testing which materials work best

title: Partager nos découvertes
oneGoal: Students will communicate their scientific observations and discoveries to classmates using words and drawings
decisionPoints: What sharing format is most comfortable and successful for Grade 1 students?
Should students share individual discoveries or work in pairs to present findings?
Are students ready for formal presentations or should we use informal sharing circles?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by developing scientific communication skills and building confidence in sharing learning
realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists share their discoveries with others, like how we tell family about interesting things we learned

title: Scientifiques dans la nature
oneGoal: Students will apply their observation and safety skills to explore natural objects and phenomena outdoors (extension)
decisionPoints: What outdoor observation activities are safe and manageable for classroom groups?
Should we focus on plants, rocks, weather, or a combination of natural elements?
Are students ready for independent outdoor observation or need structured guidance?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - applies all learned skills to natural science exploration outside the classroom
realWorldConnection: Understanding that science happens everywhere, especially in nature where we can observe weather, plants, and animals

title: Questions de scientifiques curieux
oneGoal: Students will learn to ask scientific questions that can be investigated through safe observation and simple testing (extension)
decisionPoints: Which question formats are most natural and productive for Grade 1 scientific thinking?
Should we model question-asking or encourage students to generate their own questions?
Are students ready for distinguishing testable from non-testable questions?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - develops inquiry skills by encouraging scientific questioning and curiosity
realWorldConnection: Understanding that asking questions leads to learning, just like how we ask questions to learn about new places or activities

title: Mini-laboratoire à la maison
oneGoal: Students will identify safe science exploration opportunities they can pursue at home with family supervision (extension)
decisionPoints: Which home science activities are safest and require minimal special materials?
Should we focus on observation activities or simple experiments for home exploration?
Are students ready for taking home science responsibilities or need continued classroom practice?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - extends scientific learning beyond school by connecting with family science exploration
realWorldConnection: Understanding that science learning continues at home through safe kitchen experiments, nature walks, and careful observation

title: Aider les autres à être sécuritaires
oneGoal: Students will teach safety rules to younger students or family members, demonstrating their scientific safety knowledge (extension)
decisionPoints: What teaching format allows students to share safety knowledge most effectively?
Should students focus on general safety or specific science safety when teaching others?
Are students ready for peer teaching responsibilities and modeling good behavior?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - consolidates safety learning by having students teach and model safe scientific practices
realWorldConnection: Understanding that we can help keep others safe by sharing what we know, like teaching siblings about playground safety

title: Nos outils de scientifiques à la maison
oneGoal: Students will identify common household items that can be used safely as science tools with adult supervision (extension)
decisionPoints: Which household items are safest and most effective for science exploration?
Should we focus on measuring tools, observation aids, or experiment materials?
Are students ready for independent identification of science tools or need guided examples?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - connects classroom science tools with accessible home alternatives for continued learning
realWorldConnection: Understanding that science tools are all around us, like using kitchen measuring cups or flashlights for exploration

title: Célébration des petits scientifiques
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their scientific skills and safety knowledge in a celebration showcase for families and other classes (extension)
decisionPoints: What demonstration format best showcases the range of scientific skills students have developed?
Should the celebration include live demonstrations, displays, or interactive stations?
How can we ensure every student feels proud of their scientific growth and learning?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates complete unit learning while building scientific confidence and community connections
realWorldConnection: Sharing our scientific learning with families and showing how we can safely explore and discover the world around us
